source_snapshot.title: fix(upgrade): stage downloads under IX_HOME, not TEMP
source_snapshot.body:
## Why

#349 is a Windows install that died after extraction because TEMP arrived in 8.3 short form (`[local-path] on a profile named `[local-path] 10`. The reporter confirmed that pointing `TEMP`/`TMP` at a path without a space let the same install finish.

#352 moved `install.ps1`'s scratch off TEMP for that reason — and said so in its own comment:

> Note `ix upgrade` still stages through `os.tmpdir()` (upgrade.ts), which on Windows is TEMP verbatim. If this class is real, it is unfixed there.

This is that half. It is the worse of the two places for the failure to bite: a failed install leaves a machine with no Ix on it, but a **failed upgrade breaks an install that was working** — which is exactly the shape of #385.

## What changed

Both download directories move to `IX_HOME`, joining the staging and backup directories already there. `IX_HOME` comes from `USERPROFILE` in its long form. `mkdirSync(IX_HOME)` first, because a first upgrade after a manual install can reach this before anything has created it.

`sweepUpgradeOrphans` learns `.cli-download-` and `.compass-download-`. Leaving TEMP also leaves the OS's own cleanup, so without this an upgrade killed mid-download parks a multi-MB archive in `~/.ix` forever.

The prefixes are deliberately `-download-` and not `-backup-`: `recover()` renames the newest `.cli-backup-*` over the install directory, and an archive must never be a candidate for that. There is already a test pinning that reasoning for `install.ps1`'s zip; this adds the matching one.

## The part I nearly broke

**The sweep call had to move above the download.** It sat between the download and the extract, which was safe only while the scratch lived in `os.tmpdir()`. Once the sweep reclaims `.cli-download-*`, from that position it deletes the archive it is about to extract — breaking *every* upgrade on every platform, not just Windows.

Caught while tracing the ordering rather than by a test, so there is now a test for it. Above the download, the sweep also puts an interrupted install back even when the download then fails, which the old order could not do. The compass branch already had this ordering; the CLI branch was the odd one out.

## Tests

724 green. Two new cases: an interrupted download's scratch is reclaimed, and a download directory is not treated as an install worth recovering.

`npm run lint` — 0 errors (38 pre-existing warnings). The now-unused `tmpdir` import is dropped.

## Not verified

No Windows machine here, so the 8.3 path itself is still unreproduced — see the note on #349 about the mechanism never having been pinned down. What this does is take the upgrade path off TEMP entirely, which fixes the failure under every reading of it.

Refs #349

commits.message:
fix(upgrade): stage downloads under IX_HOME, not TEMP

#349 is a Windows install that died after extraction because TEMP arrived in
8.3 short form (`[local-path] on a profile named `[local-path] 10`;
the reporter confirmed that pointing TEMP and TMP at a path without a space let
the same install finish. #352 moved install.ps1's scratch off TEMP for that
reason, and said in its own comment that `ix upgrade` still stages through
`os.tmpdir()` — which on Windows is TEMP verbatim — so if the class is real it
is unfixed there.

It is the worse of the two places for it to bite: a failed install leaves a
machine with no Ix on it, but a failed upgrade breaks an install that was
working.

Both download directories move to `IX_HOME`, which comes from USERPROFILE in
its long form, joining the staging and backup directories that were already
there. `mkdirSync(IX_HOME)` first, because a first upgrade after a manual
install may reach this before anything has created it.

Leaving TEMP also leaves the OS's own cleanup, so `sweepUpgradeOrphans` learns
the two new prefixes — otherwise an upgrade killed mid-download parks a
multi-MB archive in ~/.ix forever. They are deliberately `-download-` and not
`-backup-`: `recover()` renames the newest `.cli-backup-*` over the install
directory, and an archive must never be a candidate for that.

**The sweep call had to move above the download.** It sat between the download
and the extract, which was safe only while the scratch lived in os.tmpdir();
now that the sweep reclaims `.cli-download-*`, from that position it would
delete the archive it was about to extract and break every upgrade. Above the
download it also puts an interrupted install back even when the download then
fails, which the old order could not do. The compass branch already had this
ordering.

Refs #349

fix(upgrade): make the sweep-before-download order structural, not a comment

The PR notes the sweep call had to move above the download and says there is
now a test for it. There was not: the two new cases pin which prefixes the
sweep reclaims, but the ordering lived inline in the command action where no
test could reach it. Moving the call back below the download — which breaks
every upgrade on every platform, since the sweep then deletes the archive it
is about to extract — left all 724 tests passing.

Both call sites now go through `prepareDownloadDir()`, which does mkdir,
sweep, mkdtemp in that order and is directly testable. Three cases cover it:
an earlier run's scratch is reclaimed while the new one survives, an
interrupted install is restored before any download happens, and IX_HOME is
created when a manual install never did. Inverting the order inside the
helper fails all three.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(upgrade): bound the sweep's new reach into IX_HOME

Moving the download scratch under IX_HOME put it inside sweepUpgradeOrphans'
range, and hoisting the sweep above the download made its destructive half
run on upgrades that install nothing. Two consequences, both new:

**A failed download could delete the only working compass.**
cleanupCompassSwap:615 tests `index.html` rather than a bare existsSync, and
its comment says why: a compass/ holding only a .version is a real state, and
a bare existsSync "would call that 'back in place' and drop a backup the
caller had just told the user to go and rescue". recover() used exactly that
bare test, so the two disagreed on precisely that state — recover declined to
restore over the husk, then the loop deleted the backup. Preserved by the
swap's cleanup, destroyed by the sweep. On main this only fired after a
successful download; above the download, an offline `ix upgrade` was enough.

recover() now takes the file that proves the thing is real — index.html for
the compass, dist/cli/main.js for the install — so the two agree.

**A concurrent `ix upgrade` deleted the first run's in-flight download.**
The scratch used to live in os.tmpdir() where no sweep could match it; under
IX_HOME it was collectable for the whole 300s curl timeout. A second terminal,
or bootstrap.sh re-running `ix upgrade` when it finds compass missing, would
remove the archive mid-download — and on POSIX the unlink is silent and curl
still exits 0, so the victim fails at the extract on a download it completed.

Download directories now carry their pid (`.cli-download-<pid>-<rand>`) and
the sweep skips one whose process is still addressable. Unparseable names are
treated as dead so the pre-pid naming stays collectable. Downloads only —
staging/backup carry no pid and their reclaim behaviour is left alone.

Also: the two bare rmSync calls become rmQuiet. rmQuiet exists because Windows
rmSync does not retry and "an AV or indexer handle ... is enough to throw" —
and this PR moves those directories from TEMP into the user profile, where
scanning and indexing are the norm. The compass one runs on the success path,
where a throw skips writeCache and leaves the update notice firing for the
version just installed.

Six new cases, each verified against its bug: reverting recover() to the bare
existsSync fails two, and removing the live-pid guard fails another.

732 green, lint clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(upgrade): sweep orphans on every upgrade, not only when one is available

Both sweep calls sit behind "something needs updating" — one inside the CLI
branch, one inside the compass branch, the latter existing precisely as the
fallback for the former. #376 then tightened the compass gate to skip
release-bundled compasses, which is every install from v0.9.3 on. So a user on
the latest CLI with a release compass now runs `ix upgrade` and reclaims
nothing, and an interrupted swap is never restored.

That matters most for this PR: the archives it teaches the sweep about are
multi-MB, and the stated reason for sweeping them is that leaving os.tmpdir()
also left the OS's own cleanup. A sweep that only runs when an update happens
to be available does not deliver that.

One readdir of ~/.ix when there is nothing to do. The calls inside
prepareDownloadDir stay — that is where the sweep-before-scratch ordering is
enforced — and simply find nothing.

753 green, lint clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

reviews.body:
Taking the upgrade path off TEMP is right, and the reasoning for `-download-` over `-backup-` is correct — `recover()` renames the newest `.cli-backup-*` over the install directory, so an archive must never match that prefix.

**One gap, fixed in c8754ba.** The PR calls the sweep-above-download move "the part I nearly broke" and says "there is now a test for it". There wasn't. The two new cases pin *which prefixes the sweep reclaims*, which is what makes the ordering matter, but not the ordering itself — that lived inline in the command action where no test reaches it. I moved the call back below the download and all 724 tests passed, on a change that breaks every upgrade on every platform because the sweep then deletes the archive it is about to extract.

Both call sites now go through `prepareDownloadDir(ixHome, installDir, prefix)`, which does mkdir → sweep → mkdtemp. The order is inside one testable function instead of duplicated across two sites as a comment. Three cases: an earlier run's scratch is reclaimed while the one just created survives, an interrupted install is restored before any download happens, and IX_HOME is created when a manual install never did. Inverting the order inside the helper fails all three.

Worth noting the compass branch got the same treatment, so it no longer sweeps and then separately mkdirs — one shape on both paths.

727 green, lint clean.

Retracting my earlier approval — a deeper review found two correctness regressions introduced by moving the scratch into `IX_HOME`, one of which is data loss.

## Blocking: a failed download can delete the user's only working compass

`cleanupCompassSwap:615` tests `existsSync(join(compassDir, "index.html"))` and its comment is explicit about why: a `compass/` holding only a `.version` is a real state, and a bare `existsSync` "would call that 'back in place' and drop a backup the caller had just told the user to go and rescue."

`recover()` inside `sweepUpgradeOrphans` uses exactly that bare `existsSync(dest)`. So with `compass/` left as a `.version`-only husk and `.compass-backup-1234` holding the only real bundle, `recover()` declines to restore, and the loop below then deletes the backup.

On `main` that sweep ran *after* a successful download, so an offline run exited before reaching it and the backup survived for the next attempt. Hoisting the sweep above `curl` means **a run that installs nothing now destroys it** — the user sees only "[error] Failed to download", and `ix view` is permanently blank with no copy left on disk.

The two tests can't see this because they never construct the husk. Aligning `recover`'s test with `cleanupCompassSwap`'s (`index.html`, not bare `existsSync`) fixes it and makes the two agree.

## Blocking: concurrent `ix upgrade` deletes an in-flight download

The scratch moved from `os.tmpdir()`, where no sweep could match it, into `IX_HOME` with a swept prefix. Process A creates `.cli-download-AAAAAA` and starts a curl with a 300s timeout; process B — a second terminal, or `bootstrap.sh` re-running `ix upgrade` when it finds compass missing — calls `prepareDownloadDir` and deletes A's directory wholesale. On Linux/macOS curl's fd stays valid so A exits 0, then `tar -xzf` hits a missing path and A reports "Failed to extract CLI update" on a good download.

`.cli-staging-<pid>` has the same shape on main, but its window is the few seconds of extraction; this one is the whole download. Some ownership marker (pid in the name, skipped when that pid is live) would close both.

## Worth addressing

- `prepareDownloadDir` in the compass branch is the first filesystem write under `IX_HOME` and sits *outside* the try/catch that deliberately keeps compass failures non-fatal. On an unwritable `~/.ix` this turns "[!!] Compass extract failed / ix view keeps working" into a hard abort that also skips `writeCache`.
- Two bare `rmSync` calls (959, 1264) skip the retry treatment `rmQuiet` exists for — and this PR moves those directories into the user profile, where AV and indexer handles are the norm, which is precisely the case `rmQuiet`'s comment describes.

## One question before this lands

#349's reporter is on `[local-path] 10` and their confirmed workaround was pointing TEMP at a space-free path. This moves the scratch from `[local-path] (no space — 8.3 aliases never contain one) to `[local-path] 10\.ix\.cli-download-...` (space). If the failure is space-driven rather than short-path-driven, the upgrade path now has the space where it previously didn't. "Refs #349" rather than "Fixes" is the right call, and the PR is honest that it's unreproduced — but "fixes the failure under every reading of it" doesn't hold under the space reading. Nothing in the suite sets `IX_HOME` to a path with a space.

Taking the upgrade path off TEMP is still right, and the `-download-` vs `-backup-` prefix reasoning is correct. It's the sweep's new reach that needs bounding.

Addressed in 5432c49 and b4d9c00, and rebased onto main now that #391 has landed.

**The data-loss path.** `recover()` now takes the file that proves the thing is real — `index.html` for the compass, `cli/dist/cli/main.js` for the install — so it applies the same test `cleanupCompassSwap` already applies. The two no longer disagree about a husk, so a torn swap restores the backup instead of the sweep deleting it. Verified: reverting to the bare `existsSync` fails two of the new cases.

**The concurrency window.** Download directories carry their pid (`.cli-download-<pid>-<rand>`) and the sweep skips one whose process is still addressable — `process.kill(pid, 0)`, treating EPERM as live. Unparseable names are treated as dead so the pre-pid naming stays collectable, and the guard is scoped to download prefixes so staging/backup reclaim behaviour is untouched. Verified: removing the guard fails the live-process case.

**The two bare `rmSync` calls** are now `rmQuiet`, which is the whole reason that helper exists — and this PR is what moves those directories from TEMP into the user profile.

**One more, found while composing the two PRs** (b4d9c00): both sweep calls sit behind "something needs updating", and #391 tightened the compass gate to skip release-bundled compasses — which is every install from v0.9.3 on. So on a healthy current install neither would fire and nothing would ever be reclaimed, which defeats the reason for sweeping the downloads at all. There is now one unconditional sweep at the top of a real `ix upgrade`; the calls inside `prepareDownloadDir` stay, since that is where the ordering invariant lives.

753 green on the rebased result, lint clean.

**Still open, and deliberately not resolved here:** whether #349 is space-driven or short-path-driven. The scratch now sits under `[local-path] 10\.ix\...`, which contains the space, where the TEMP path it replaces did not. `Refs #349` is the right framing until someone reproduces it — worth keeping the issue open rather than closing it on this.
